zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 油價推升美債通膨補償，信用市場恢復發行

能源設施再度遭襲，抵銷荷姆茲海峽通行略有改善的利多，美國市場開市後，油價與美債通膨補償同步上升。布蘭特原油上漲3.334%至$99.49，WTI上漲3.181%至$94.39。2年與10年期殖利率各上升2個基點，分別至4.39%與4.80%，30年期上升1個基點至5.25%。

10年期實質殖利率維持2.43%，名目殖利率的漲幅來自損益兩平通膨率升至2.37%。能源成本增加聯準會繼續觀望的風險，但曲線變化有限：2年與10年期利差維持41個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄1個基點至86個基點。當日貨幣市場定價顯示，9月升息機率仍在50%以上。

假日後，借款人仍找到大量買盤。18家美國投資級發行人募集$386億，雖不及近年勞動節後首個交易日的速度，仍是今年第三忙碌的一天。投資級利差小幅收窄，高收益與強勢貨幣新興市場債利差近乎不變。貸款市場既有借款人爭取降低利差，也有新的收購融資；塞內加爾、Vista Land與Sophos則仍需透過各自的債權協商處理資金需求。

需求端的訊號較為分歧。美國小企業與家庭信心轉弱，澳洲消費與企業調查普遍承壓，日本薪資成長強勁，消費卻持平。接下來的物價數據將顯示燃料成本如何擴散，而信心與支出數據則反映家庭、企業承受能源及利率同時上升的能力。

## 燃料供應惡化，美國信心走弱

沙烏地表示南部多處設施遭襲後起火、有人受傷，營運已停止；伊朗支持的胡塞組織宣稱發動新攻擊。美國交易時段，Fox報導美軍攻擊哈爾克島及賈斯克附近，伊朗國營電視警告科威特與巴林碼頭附近油輪船員離船，因可能成為目標。生產、裝載與航運同受威脅，使布蘭特升破稍早約$98結算價。

一艘上月初裝載的卡達LNG船，成為7月以來首艘可觀察到通過荷姆茲海峽出口的船，讓通航談判之外出現實際進展。不過，單一船次尚不足以抵銷新停工帶來的影響。歐洲儲氣率目前67%，低於同期常態83%。奈及利亞Dangote煉油廠滿載運轉，盡量增加輸歐柴油與航空燃油，有助成品油供應，卻無法填補天然氣缺口。

美國NFIB小企業樂觀指數由99.8降至98.7，低於99.3預估。中古車價格月減0.9%，前期下降1.4%，年增率由1.3%降至0.4%。雖然月跌幅收斂，價格仍在下降，與企業信心轉弱一起，呈現能源以外較溫和的需求及物價訊號。

紐約聯準銀行8月調查顯示，一年及五年通膨預期維持3.6%與3.0%，三年由3.3%降至3.2%。受訪者預期汽油更貴，但較廣泛的通膨期間未一致上升。預期失業率提高的程度為2020年4月以來最強，跨年齡、所得及教育皆惡化。自認失去工作的機率下降，失業後再找到工作的信心卻也下降；目前與未來財務，以及信用取得評估均轉弱。

實際借款仍強：7月消費信用增$180.6億，高於$117億預估及修正後$145.6億前值。借款可能支撐支出，也可能彌補財務壓力，總額無法區分，因此信心轉弱不等於家庭融資已收縮。

加拿大對數百種美國商品15%至50%報復關稅生效，許多鋼品由25%升至50%，也涵蓋機車、化妝品及起司。這提高加拿大進口成本、降低美國生產者在當地競爭力，並不是直接提高美國進口價格。

股票反映需求差異。S&P 500跌0.584%，半導體漲1.3004%；黃金期貨跌0.6389%至$4,401.50，即使美元指數跌0.355%至98.808。AI需求仍有支持，未見所有資產一致轉向防禦。

## 日本薪資強，其他市場消費者卻更吃力

日本7月名目薪資年增4.7%，高於預估的3.8%與6月修正值4%，創1997年以來最快。薪資已連續六個月成長逾3%，為34年最長紀錄。以不含租金的通膨指標調整後，實質薪資增加2.4%，約為五年最高；底薪成長4.1%，但排除獎金、加班與樣本變化的穩定全職薪資指標，增幅較溫和，為2.7%。

日本工會聯合會協商的加薪幅度，連續第三年超過5%，本財年平均最低工資達每小時¥1,177，調幅為歷來第二大。企業獲利增加，加上金融、建築及物流業缺工，讓薪資成長不只依靠獎金，但消費支出尚未同樣強勁。

第2季實質GDP年化成長率由1.1%上修至1.4%，仍低於1.8%預估。企業投資季減幅由1.2%縮小至0.9%，是上修的原因之一，但並未轉為成長，消費也持平。政府支出年化增加6.9%，部分來自免費學校午餐將支出由家庭轉至政府；釋出石油儲備則壓低公共存貨。名目GDP年化成長5.5%。

5年期日債投標倍數由4.15降至3.42，接近12個月平均3.44，得標價差由0.02擴大至0.04，期貨一度下跌。SMBC Nikko的Miki Den認為，結果略弱但符合預期：上午殖利率已下降，美元兌日圓波動也使部分買家觀望。標售仍順利完成，但薪資強勁增加升息風險，使投資人較不急於鎖定政策敏感天期的殖利率。

日圓一度升至每美元153.53，但最新月度資料並不顯示所有日本投資人都把資金轉回國內。8月外國短期債淨賣出¥1.02兆，長期債淨賣出¥1,430億，合計為五個月最大海外債淨賣出。壽險賣出長債¥1,373億，投信賣出¥301億；退休基金卻買入外債¥2.33兆、外股¥5,671億。整體外股買入¥1.3兆，為3月¥2.22兆以來最多。

德意志銀行的Shoki Omori表示，今年累計至8月，壽險大致未參與外債淨賣出，銀行小幅減碼，退休信託仍持續買入。厚生勞動大臣Kenichiro Ueno也說，GPIF仍在評估是否需要檢討配置，尚未採用更高的本國資產比重。壽險單月賣出與退休基金買入並存，資金流向仍因機構而異。

澳洲信心普遍轉弱。Westpac消費者信心指數下降5.2%至84.4，對家庭財務相較一年前的評估下降9.2%，房貸族信心下降14%，大額採購意願指標下降18%。全球成本上升，加上燃油稅暫時減半措施結束，使汽油每公升超過A$2。NAB企業信心下降2點至−8，營運狀況下降5點至−1，為六年來首次負值，主要受到獲利指標下降10點影響。

澳洲央行副總裁Andrew Hauser表示，問題在於目前緊縮是否已足夠，而非必然再升息。Sarah Hunter認為，通膨若高於預測可能需要進一步緊縮，但季度資料比波動較大的月度數據更有參考性。政策利率目前4.35%，房市疲弱仍不足以決定下一步：8月房價下降0.9%，連跌第五個月，比3月低3.6%。HSBC將高點至低點的跌幅預測由8%擴大至13%，Westpac則由不變轉為預估下跌4.6%。

Hunter表示，央行正在觀察Bathla與私人信貸的情況，目前未見系統性壓力蔓延至銀行，經濟衰退也不是基本預測。

中國出口年增25.0%，符合預期，較前期23.9%加速；進口增加28.2%，低於30%預估，但高於前期27.5%。貿易順差由$1,125億增至$1,190.9億，1至8月累計達$8,055.1億。前八個月高科技出口額增加42.9%，其中半導體金額成長逾一倍，數量卻僅增加4.1%。

汽車市場呈現內外需求差異：國內零售下降24%至154萬輛，出口卻增加78%至88.8萬輛，占總銷售38%。比亞迪將海外銷售目標由150萬輛提高至190萬至200萬輛。整體對美貿易順差由$280億增至$291.8億，出口增加34.4%、進口增加17.8%。數據公布後，人民幣持平，股市小幅上漲。

智利CPI月增0.6%，高於預估的0.3%與前期的0.1%；年增率由3.5%升至4.1%，超過3%目標上下1個百分點的範圍。運輸價格上漲1.6%，食品與非酒精飲料上漲1.4%，13類中有九類上漲，通信價格則下降0.3%。

Rosanna Costa領導的智利央行委員會一致決議，第六次維持利率4.5%。央行警告中東風險增加、內需疲弱可能延續更久，但投資展望仍佳，兩年期通膨預期也維持3%。7月經濟活動下降1.7%，礦業、商業及服務業均偏弱。其他市場也面臨類似取捨：哥倫比亞通膨超出預期、升至兩年高點，南非第2季則結束連續六季成長，產出轉弱未必能立即換來降息空間。

## 密集開市供給仍吸引債券與貸款買盤

18家投資級借款人共募集$386億。以勞動節後首個交易日比較，家數為2020年以來最少、金額為三年最低，2024年與去年分別有29家及27家，但總額仍高於該日七年平均。TD的Hans Mikkelsen認為，上午市場疲弱可能使部分企業延後發行。

GSK募集$65億，部分用於再融資Nuvalent收購債務；UBS、Bank of Montreal及Ares Management的私人信貸基金也籌措資金。今年投資級累計發行達$1.53兆，比2020年同期紀錄高8.8%。歐洲20家發行人募集約€277億，為6月9日以來最忙碌的一天。亞洲準備發行的企業包括Mizuho、Commonwealth Bank of Australia與Malayan Banking，Olympus也已委任銀行。

Amazon委任JPMorgan、Barclays、HSBC與NatWest安排首次英鎊發債，考慮3年、6年、12年及19年期，尚未完成定價。公司今年已發行逾$920億等值債務，資本支出計畫達$2,200億，主要投入AI。若交易完成，英國投資人將多一組涵蓋長天期的公司債選擇。

EDF的€10億綠色混合資本債吸引逾€30億訂單，殖利率指引由約5.75%降至5.375%。新券於2031年首次可贖回，資金用於法國核電維護與延役；每年相關支出超過€50億，這些機組供應法國逾三分之二電力。評等機構可將部分融資視為股本，有助資產負債表，但法律順位仍屬次順位。EDF另擬贖回€8.5億2020年混合資本債，並買回€12.5億2021年次順位社會債。

美國至少推出18筆貸款，為5月18日以來最多，其中至少七筆爭取重新定價。Global Medical Response的$29億方案，希望定在基準利率加2.75至3個百分點，低於既有2032年到期貸款的3.25個百分點。Heartland Dental希望將$25億、同樣2032年到期的貸款利差降低0.5個百分點；Freeport與WHP Global則分別推出$21.8億與$18.6億方案。若完成，借款人可降低信用利差，但總浮動利率仍受基準利率影響。

截至9月2日當週，貸款基金流入為1月以來最強，CLO需求也增加，收購融資則提供重新定價交易之外的選擇。Bank of America與Deutsche Bank主導€28億方案，支持Platinum Equity收購Nestlé水事業Peranel的50%股權，品牌包括Perrier與S.Pellegrino。七年期方案包含€16億等值美元及€12億歐元B類定期貸款，約13家銀行承銷。投資人承擔的是該水事業的風險，包括需求疲弱、水處理調查與訴訟，而非單憑Nestlé品牌即可評估。

其他收購融資包括Veritas收購Saber Power Services的$12.5億貸款，以及KKR收購Integer的$21億貸款。後者初步條件為基準利率加2.75至3個百分點、發行價每美元99.5美分。摩根大通估計，美國待融資的槓桿收購交易約$920億，為2007年以來最多；歐洲則接近€400億、約$460億，為2021年以來最多。這些估計尚未計入至多$800億的美國資料中心融資。

歐洲後續供給包括EQT收購Intertek的£50億融資，以及Recordati的€60億高收益債。市場預期，較受歡迎的單B級交易初始利差約為Euribor加325至350個基點，可能收窄至300個基點；吸引力較低的交易則可能需要375至425個基點。這是對後續定價的預估，交易條件仍待確定。

Reliance擬發行五年期AAA債，票息7.47%，低於週一同評等平均7.87%。先前₹1,250億的上限，分為₹1,000億基本規模與₹250億增額，由Axis、ICICI、HDFC及YES Bank安排。印度國內公司債借款年減約11%至₹8.9兆，截至7月的一年內，新銀行貸款利率下降29個基點；這筆交易將顯示債券能否重新提供有競爭力的融資條件。

AlphaGrep則以成本較高的證券融資，替代受限制的銀行資金。公司已完成₹20億、約$2,100萬的一年期A+債，票息10.5%，高於同級9.45%，資金支持AI、機器學習基礎設施及零售業務。印度央行限制銀行對自營交易商的曝險，使公司轉向商業本票與債券；6月底₹289億銀行保證預計隨到期逐步退出。

外國借款人也轉向成本較低的人民幣資金，熊貓債發行額增加74%至創紀錄的CN¥2,250億。前中國人民銀行官員Ma Jun已與三家有興趣的吉爾吉斯銀行討論發債，但尚未完成交易。分銷方面，UniCredit買入貸款及Schuldschein平台VC Trade的少數股權，保留增持空間，並計畫在集團網絡使用該平台。

## 債務管理者在更高殖利率取得需求

英國發行£42.5億、票息5.375%、2056年1月到期的公債，殖利率達5.8168%，創債務管理局（DMO）1998年成立以來標售或聯貸發行的最高水準。訂單達£872億，71%來自本地投資人；定價較票息4.25%的2055年到期券高0.75個基點。龐大訂單讓政府順利取得長期資金，但代價是更高的借款成本。

長天期普通公債占本財年£2,460億發債計畫不到10%。英國預算責任署（OBR）預估，債息支出將達£1,090億，占公共支出8.4%，融資成本仍是預算的一大壓力。

Andrew Bailey在國會表示，市場反映的部分緊縮幅度來自能源風險溢價，英國央行並沒有無條件升息的計畫。目前定價反映年底前升息25個基點，2027年再升息兩次。Bailey承認，7月以來的數據略強於預測，經濟活動仍有韌性。官員對通膨的看法則有分歧：Dave Ramsden認為本地通膨壓力相對溫和，Megan Greene警告，油價衝擊若持續，可能使通膨預期更難消退。

義大利的成長前景改善，卻也引發新增支出的要求。Giancarlo Giorgetti表示，成長假設為0.8%，甚至可能接近1%，高於原先的0.6%；Matteo Salvini則要求增加約€200億支出。政府債務已超過GDP的130%，赤字為3.1%，新增收入若被支出吸收，較好的成長未必能減少借款需求。

Bessent在Southern Methodist University表示，擴大舊券買回，是為了平抑市場對政府償付能力的疑慮；他認為這些疑慮缺乏根據，卻愈來愈影響交易。摩根大通Jay Barry團隊發現，20年期公債相對10年及30年期已異常昂貴，反映投資人提前布局官方買盤。買回規模與資金來源因此可能在實際執行前，就改變各天期的相對價格。週二三年期標售殖利率為4.474%，高於前次4.291%；短期附息債的借款成本提高，長端需求仍待後續標售檢驗。

## 困境再融資取決於現金來源與債權

塞內加爾Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo向議員表示，政府希望延長到期日並重新協商利率，將其稱為債務期限調整，而非重整。他同時披露，截至2024年底，政府對5,425名請款者積欠CFA1.96兆、約$35億。政府需要處理的現金缺口，因此不僅是國際債券的利息支付。

塞內加爾債券價格約為每美元52美分，從上週不到50美分回升。Seaport的Sebastian Vargas引述投資人估計，回收價值可能為40至45美分；Tellimer的Stuart Culverhouse則估計，溫和展延可保留接近70至略高於70美分的價值，若本金與票息削減較深，回收價值可能在45美分附近或以下。這些仍是情境估計，尚非正式交換條件。

損失如何分攤也是談判重點。塞內加爾約有$50億國際債，若本地債不納入調整，損失將更集中於外部債權人。Allan Gray的Thalia Petousis指出，IMF對外部債務可持續性的分析，與對政府總融資需求的分析並不相同；後者可能意味著外債需要承擔更大的損失。

菲律賓央行表示，政府借款並未排擠民間企業融資，但債券發行仍集中於大型、高評等公司。截至6月底，公部門貸款為₱2,540億，占銀行信用的1.4%，年減2.3%；銀行持有的政府證券與民間貸款則同步增加。央行較關注融資價格，必要時可減少回收流動性的規模。

Vista Land面臨的再融資壓力則較大。Manuel Villar旗下這家建商考慮出售包括兩座商場在內的資產，籌措至多₱150億、約$2.4億，搭配銀行融資、營運現金流與資本市場資金。公司票息7.25%、2027年7月到期的債券，已從6月5日每美元47.5美分的低點回升至80.3美分；票息9.375%、2029年7月到期的債券，則從5月20日的33.9美分升至61.9美分。售產計畫使償債資金來源更具體，但尚未完成出售。

Vista在2027年7月及2029年7月分別有$4.2億、$4.5億債務到期，2026年剩餘本地到期債務為₱122億。CreditSights認為，2027年底前的本地債務大致可控，但海外再融資仰賴銀行與售產；若兩者未能落實，公司很可能需要重整，目前負債管理交易仍非基本情境。Ayala Land與SM Prime持續取得銀行及債券資金，也說明Vista的財務與治理問題，不宜等同於整個市場缺乏資金。

Thoma Bravo再度嘗試修改並延長Sophos的$21億貸款，該筆貸款於2027年3月到期，由Goldman Sachs主導協商。先前即使有望大幅提高收益，多家私人貸款人仍拒絕參與。較高票息、分期攤還與更嚴格條款都是協商選項，尚未成為已同意的保障。這是未來數年約$90億軟體業到期債務中最急迫的一筆，貸款人仍在評估槓桿及AI對業務的衝擊。

Goldman與Deutsche提供包含AT1的法國債券組合，客戶可透過現券、總報酬交換等工具，建立對應不同政治結果的部位。這些交易安排並非銀行對選舉結果的預測。近幾個月，法國銀行債在多數天期的風險溢價擴大，與整體AT1市場利差普遍收窄的走勢不同。

Jefferies管理基金在$5億倫敦訴訟指控Radiant World偽造鐵礦砂發票，8月底提告後取得全球凍結令；新公開細節仍是指控，不是詐欺判決。文件真實性及可回收資產，比整體利差方向更能決定這項債權。

## 通膨與買回細節將檢驗開市後需求

接下來的美國數據將顯示能源漲價是否向其他項目擴散。9月10日PPI預估整體月增0.4%、核心月增0.3%；初領失業救濟金人數預估20.5萬，前期為20.6萬。11日CPI預估月增0.4%，高於前期0.1%；核心月增率預估0.2%，年增率則由2.5%降至2.4%。若非能源項目也普遍漲價，將增加聯準會16日採取行動的理由；若核心通膨與勞動數據偏弱，則較有利於維持觀望。

歐洲央行9月10日、日本央行17至18日的會議，面對的內需條件不同。市場預期日本升息25個基點至1.25%；薪資數據強勁之後，投資人也將關注本次會議是否改變後續升息步調。

財政部將於9日公布10日買回10至20年期美債的細節，另有9日的10年期及10日的30年期標售。官方承諾買回至少$40億，Wrightson的Lou Crandall認為可能達$50億至$60億，Morgan Stanley估計實務上的融資上限接近$100億。市場需分辨資金來自增發短券還是降低現金餘額，也需區分買回上限與最終接受金額。若實際安排低於預期，提前反映買盤的相對價值部位，包括長端交換利差，可能回吐先前走勢。

信用市場方面，Amazon英鎊債最快9月9日定價。SoftBank雖考慮籌措$100億至$200億高收益融資，9月14至17日安排的仍是非交易路演，發行條件尚待確認。塞內加爾2048年到期境外債將於9月13日支付$3,370萬，屆時可觀察政府在債務協商期間的實際支付能力。Sophos則將於9月10日召開電話會議，貸款承諾截止日為22日；其展延結果仍取決於貸款人是否接受個別條件。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Oil lifts Treasury breakevens as credit markets reopen

Renewed attacks on energy facilities outweighed a limited improvement in Hormuz passage, lifting oil and Treasury inflation compensation as US markets reopened. Brent reached $99.49, up 3.334%, and WTI $94.39, up 3.181%. The 2- and 10-year yields each rose 2 basis points to 4.39% and 4.80%, while the 30-year gained 1 to 5.25%.

Ten-year real yields held at 2.43%; the nominal move came from breakevens rising to 2.37%. The curve changed little—2s10s held at 41 basis points and 2s30s narrowed 1 to 86—even as energy made waiting on inflation riskier. Money-market reporting still put a September Fed increase above 50% probability, not a settled outcome.

Borrowers found substantial demand after the holiday. Eighteen US IG issuers raised $38.6 billion, a slower Labor Day reopening than recent years but still the year's third-busiest day. IG spreads tightened modestly; HY and hard-currency EM barely changed. Loan borrowers sought lower margins and new acquisition financing, while Senegal, Vista Land and Sophos still needed creditor-specific solutions.

Domestic demand did not uniformly support the inflation pressure. US small-business and household confidence weakened, Australia reported broad strain and Japan's strong wage growth accompanied flat consumption. The next price releases must show whether dearer fuel is spreading, rather than assume that households and businesses can comfortably absorb both energy and higher rates.

## Fuel supply deteriorates while US confidence weakens

Saudi Arabia said attacks halted several southern facilities after fires and injuries; Iran-backed Houthis claimed fresh strikes. During the US session, Fox reported American attacks near Kharg Island and Jask. Iranian state television warned tanker crews near Kuwaiti and Bahraini piers to leave because they could be targeted. Threats to production and loading added to shipping disruption, sending Brent above the roughly $98 settlement reported earlier.

A Qatari LNG tanker loaded early last month made the first visible exit through Hormuz since July. That is actual progress beyond route negotiations, but only one cargo against new shutdowns. European storage was 67% versus a seasonal norm of 83%. Dangote's Nigerian refinery was running at capacity and maximizing diesel and jet-fuel deliveries to Europe, helping refined products without resolving the gas shortage.

US NFIB optimism fell to 98.7 from 99.8, below 99.3 consensus. Used-car prices declined 0.9% monthly after −1.4%, with annual growth slowing to 0.4% from 1.3%. The smaller monthly fall still represents component-level disinflation, alongside weaker business confidence.

The New York Fed's August consumer survey left one- and five-year inflation expectations at 3.6% and 3.0%, while three-year expectations eased to 3.2% from 3.3%. Respondents anticipated higher gasoline prices but not a uniform rise across broader horizons. Expectations of higher unemployment reached their strongest since April 2020 across age, income and education groups. Perceived job-loss risk fell, yet confidence in finding another job after a loss deteriorated. Current and expected finances and access to credit also weakened.

Actual borrowing remained strong: July consumer credit increased $18.06 billion, above $11.7 billion consensus and a revised $14.56 billion gain. It may support spending or offset financial strain; the aggregate does not distinguish the two. Weaker survey responses therefore cannot be described as an already completed contraction in household finance.

Canada's 15%–50% retaliatory tariffs took effect on hundreds of US goods, including many steel duties rising to 50% from 25%, plus motorcycles, cosmetics and cheese. They raise Canadian import costs and reduce US producers' competitiveness there, rather than directly raising US import prices.

Stocks reflected uneven demand. The S&P 500 fell 0.584%, while semiconductors gained 1.3004%. Gold futures fell 0.6389% to $4,401.50 even as DXY lost 0.355% to 98.808. AI demand retained support without a broad defensive move across assets.

## Japan's wages strengthen, but consumers elsewhere struggle

Japanese nominal wages rose 4.7% annually in July, beating 3.8% consensus and revised June growth of 4%. It was the fastest since 1997 and the sixth month above 3%, the longest run in 34 years. Real wages excluding rent inflation rose 2.4%, the most in about five years. Base pay gained 4.1%, but the stable full-time measure excluding bonuses, overtime and sampling effects rose a more moderate 2.7%.

Rengo-negotiated increases exceeded 5% for a third year, and the fiscal-year average minimum wage reached ¥1,177 an hour, the second-largest increase on record. Expanding profits and shortages in finance, construction and logistics give pay growth support beyond bonuses. Spending has yet to respond as strongly.

Q2 real GDP was revised to 1.4% annualized from 1.1%, below 1.8% consensus. Business investment fell 0.9% quarterly rather than 1.2%, explaining the upgrade without turning investment positive. Consumption was flat. Government spending rose 6.9% annualized, partly as free school lunches shifted expenditure out of households; oil-stockpile releases depressed public inventories. Nominal GDP grew 5.5% annualized.

Five-year JGB coverage fell to 3.42 from 4.15, near the 12-month average of 3.44, and the reported tail widened to 0.04 from 0.02. Futures briefly fell. SMBC Nikko's Miki Den called demand slightly weak but within expectations, citing the morning yield decline and volatile dollar-yen deterring some buyers. The auction placed the debt, but stronger wage evidence made locking in policy-sensitive yields less appealing.

The yen reached 153.53 per dollar. New monthly flow detail did not show all Japanese investors bringing funds home: August sales were ¥1.02 trillion of foreign short-term debt and ¥143 billion of long-term bonds, the largest monthly overseas-bond selling in five months. Life insurers sold ¥137.3 billion of long bonds and investment trusts ¥30.1 billion; pensions bought ¥2.33 trillion of foreign bonds and ¥567.1 billion of equities. Total foreign-equity purchases of ¥1.3 trillion were largest since March's ¥2.22 trillion.

Deutsche Bank's Shoki Omori said insurers were essentially absent from foreign-bond selling through August on a year-to-date basis, with banks modest sellers and pension trusts continuing to buy. Health Minister Kenichiro Ueno said GPIF was still deciding whether a review was needed, not adopting a higher domestic weight. Monthly insurer sales, pension inflows and changing hedge incentives are different developments, not one national liquidation trade.

Australia's confidence weakened broadly. Westpac sentiment fell 5.2% to 84.4, family finances against a year earlier 9.2%, mortgage-borrower sentiment 14% and their major-purchase assessment 18%. Petrol exceeded A$2 a liter as global costs rose and the temporary halving of excise ended. NAB confidence fell 2 points to −8; conditions dropped 5 to −1, the first negative reading in six years, led by a 10-point profitability decline.

RBA Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said the question was whether enough had been done, not that another hike was inevitable. Sarah Hunter said inflation above forecasts could require more restraint but preferred quarterly evidence to volatile monthly readings. At a 4.35% cash rate, housing weakness had not settled the decision: home values fell 0.9% in August, their fifth decline, to 3.6% below March. HSBC raised its projected peak-to-trough fall from 8% to 13%; Westpac switched from a hold forecast to 4.6%.

Hunter said the RBA was monitoring Bathla and private credit but saw no systemic stress spreading through banks; recession was not its baseline. The new information is that assessment, not another account of the developer's insolvency.

China's exports rose 25.0% annually, matching forecasts and accelerating from 23.9%. Imports gained 28.2% versus 30% expected and 27.5% previously. The surplus widened to $119.09 billion from $112.5 billion, reaching $805.51 billion for January–August. High-tech export values rose 42.9% over eight months; semiconductor values more than doubled on volume growth of only 4.1%.

Autos showed the divide between external and domestic demand. Retail sales fell 24% to 1.54 million, while exports rose 78% to 888,000, or 38% of total sales. BYD raised overseas guidance to 1.9 million–2 million from 1.5 million. The US surplus grew to $29.18 billion from $28 billion, with exports to the US up 34.4% and imports 17.8%. The yuan was flat and stocks edged higher after trade data.

Chile's CPI rose 0.6% monthly against 0.3% forecast and 0.1% previously. Annual inflation accelerated to 4.1% from 3.5%, above the 3% target's 1-percentage-point tolerance band. Transport rose 1.6%, food/nonalcoholic drinks 1.4%, and nine of 13 categories increased; communications fell 0.3%.

Rosanna Costa's board unanimously held 4.5% for a sixth meeting. It warned that Middle East risks had intensified and domestic weakness could last longer, while investment prospects remained favorable and two-year expectations anchored at 3%. July activity contracted 1.7% across mining, commerce and services. Colombia's inflation also accelerated more than expected to a two-year high, while South Africa's Q2 economy ended six quarters of growth. Weak output is not reliably delivering room to ease.

## A crowded reopening still attracts bond and loan buyers

Eighteen IG borrowers raised $38.6 billion, the fewest issuers for the post-Labor Day opening since 2020 and lowest volume in three years, compared with 29 issuers in 2024 and 27 last year. Yet the total exceeded the seven-year average for the day. TD's Hans Mikkelsen suspected weak morning markets postponed some deals.

GSK raised $6.5 billion partly to refinance Nuvalent acquisition debt; UBS, Bank of Montreal and Ares Management's private-credit fund also borrowed. Year-to-date IG issuance reached $1.53 trillion, 8.8% above the comparable 2020 record pace. Europe's 20 borrowers raised about €27.7 billion, busiest since June 9. Asian preparations included Mizuho, Commonwealth Bank of Australia and Malayan Banking, with Olympus mandating banks.

Amazon mandated JPMorgan, Barclays, HSBC and NatWest for its first sterling offering, contemplating 3-, 6-, 12- and 19-year maturities. No completed sale followed from the mandate. It has already issued over $92 billion-equivalent this year and plans $220 billion capex, mostly AI, bringing another source of corporate duration to UK investors.

EDF's €1 billion green hybrid drew over €3 billion of orders, tightening indicated yield to 5.375% from around 5.75%. First callable in 2031, it finances maintenance and life extension of French reactors, work costing over €5 billion annually across a fleet supplying more than two-thirds of French power. Partial rating-agency equity credit helps its balance sheet, although the debt remains subordinated. EDF also plans to redeem €850 million of 2020 hybrids and tender for €1.25 billion of 2021 subordinated social bonds.

At least 18 US loan deals launched, most since May 18, including seven or more repricings. Global Medical Response sought $2.9 billion at benchmark plus 2.75–3 percentage points versus 3.25 on its 2032 loan. Heartland Dental sought 0.5 percentage point less on $2.5 billion due 2032; Freeport and WHP Global proposed $2.18 billion and $1.86 billion repricings. These reduce credit margins if completed, not necessarily total floating-rate expense.

Loan-fund inflows in the week through September 2 were the strongest since January, alongside growing CLO issuance. Acquisition supply provides alternatives to repricings. Bank of America and Deutsche Bank led €2.8 billion for Platinum Equity's 50% purchase of Nestlé's water unit, Peranel, including Perrier and S.Pellegrino. The seven-year package comprises €1.6 billion-equivalent dollar and €1.2 billion euro term loan Bs, underwritten by about 13 banks. Exposure is to a business facing weak demand and water-treatment investigations and litigation, not simply Nestlé's name.

Veritas's Saber Power Services acquisition added $1.25 billion. The $2.1 billion Integer loan backing KKR's purchase was offered at benchmark plus 2.75–3 percentage points and 99.5 cents. JPMorgan's leveraged-acquisition pipeline totals about $92 billion in the US, largest since 2007, and nearly €40 billion/$46 billion in Europe, largest since 2021, excluding up to $80 billion of possible US data-center finance. It includes £5 billion for EQT's Intertek deal and €6 billion of HY bonds for Recordati. Well-regarded European single-B loans are expected around Euribor plus 325–350 basis points at launch, potentially 300, versus 375–425 for less popular names—not cleared pipeline-wide prices.

Reliance's proposed five-year AAA notes carry 7.47%, below Monday's 7.87% average for top-rated five-year debt. The previously signaled ₹125 billion maximum is ₹100 billion plus a ₹25 billion greenshoe, arranged by Axis, ICICI, HDFC and YES Bank. Domestic bond borrowing fell about 11% annually to ₹8.9 trillion while fresh bank-loan rates declined 29 basis points over the year through July, making these terms a test of renewed bond competitiveness.

AlphaGrep instead replaced constrained bank access with costlier securities. Its completed ₹2 billion/$21 million one-year A+ issue pays 10.5%, versus a 9.45% comparable yield, for AI/machine-learning infrastructure and retail businesses. RBI proprietary-trader exposure restrictions push funding toward commercial paper and debentures; ₹28.9 billion of bank guarantees at June 30 are expected to run off at expiry.

Panda issuance reached a record CN¥225 billion, up 74%, as foreign borrowers sought cheaper yuan funding. Former PBOC official Ma Jun discussed the market with three interested Kyrgyz banks, not completed deals. Separately, UniCredit bought a minority stake in loan and Schuldschein platform VC Trade, with an option to add and plans for network-wide use—a distribution investment, not another financing amount.

## Debt managers find demand at higher yields

The UK sold £4.25 billion of 5.375% January 2056 gilts at 5.8168%, the highest auction or syndication yield since the DMO's 1998 creation. Orders reached £87.2 billion, 71% domestic, and pricing was 0.75 basis points above the 4.25% 2055 gilt. Demand was strong at that price, not at the government's old financing assumptions.

Long conventional issues will be under 10% of the £246 billion fiscal-year program. OBR forecasts £109 billion of debt interest, 8.4% of public spending. Successful long funding still leaves a large budget cost.

Andrew Bailey told lawmakers some priced tightening reflected an energy-risk premium and rejected an unconditional hike plan. Markets priced one 25-basis-point move by year-end and two in 2027. He acknowledged slightly stronger-than-forecast data since July and resilient activity. Dave Ramsden called domestic inflation relatively benign; Megan Greene warned prolonged oil pressure could make expectations persistent.

Italy's Giancarlo Giorgetti said growth assumptions were 0.8%, potentially near 1%, versus an earlier 0.6%. Matteo Salvini's demand for about €20 billion extra spending competes for the revenue benefit. Debt above 130% of GDP and a 3.1% deficit mean better growth does not automatically lower borrowing.

Bessent said at Southern Methodist University that expanded old-bond buybacks aimed to cool a market driven increasingly by an unfounded inability-to-pay narrative. JPMorgan's Jay Barry and colleagues found 20-year Treasuries unusually expensive against 10s and 30s, consistent with anticipated official demand. The eventual scale and financing can therefore move relative prices before purchases. Tuesday's three-year auction yielded 4.474% versus 4.291% previously, establishing higher short-coupon funding cost without settling longer-end demand.

## Distressed refinancing turns on cash sources and creditor rights

Senegal's Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo told lawmakers the government sought reprofiling through longer maturities and renegotiated interest, not a restructuring. He disclosed CFA1.96 trillion/$3.5 billion of domestic arrears through late 2024 owed to 5,425 claimants. The cash problem extends beyond international bond service regardless of terminology.

Notes traded around 52 cents, up from below 50 last week. Seaport's Sebastian Vargas cited investor recovery estimates of 40–45 cents. Tellimer's Stuart Culverhouse valued mild reprofiling in the high 60s to low 70s, deeper principal/coupon cuts in the mid-40s or below. These are scenarios, not exchange terms. Against roughly $5 billion of international bonds, excluding local claims concentrates relief on external holders. Allan Gray's Thalia Petousis distinguished IMF external-sustainability analysis from total financing needs; the latter could require larger foreign-claim losses.

The Philippine BSP said investable funds were not crowding out private business, though issuance favored large high-rated companies. Public-entity loans were ₱254 billion at June-end, only 1.4% of bank credit and down 2.3% annually; government securities and private lending both grew. It identified financing price as the issue and could reduce liquidity drains if needed.

Vista Land's individual position is weaker. Manuel Villar's developer considers asset sales including two malls for up to ₱15 billion/$240 million, alongside banks, cash flow and markets. Its 7.25% July 2027 bonds reached 80.3 cents from a June 5 low of 47.5; 9.375% July 2029 notes reached 61.9 from 33.9 on May 20. Repayment resources are becoming more specific but disposals are not completed.

Vista owes $420 million in July 2027, $450 million in July 2029 and ₱12.2 billion locally over the rest of 2026. CreditSights saw local maturities through end-2027 as largely manageable, offshore refinancing dependent on banks and sales, and restructuring likely if those routes fail; liability management was not its base case. Ayala Land and SM Prime continued accessing banks and bonds, separating Vista's financial/governance risks from system-wide shortage.

Thoma Bravo launched another amendment-and-extension attempt for Sophos's $2.1 billion March 2027 loan, led by Goldman Sachs, after several private lenders passed despite possible steep yield increases. Higher coupons, amortization and tighter covenants are options, not agreed protections. It is the sponsor's most urgent maturity within roughly $9 billion of software debt due over the next couple of years, with lenders weighing leverage and AI disruption.

Goldman and Deutsche Bank offered French bond baskets including AT1, through cash bonds or derivatives such as total return swaps, allowing clients to position for political outcomes rather than expressing the banks' election forecasts. French bank premiums widened over much of the curve in the past month while broad AT1 mostly tightened.

A Jefferies-managed fund alleged falsified iron-ore invoices by Radiant World in a $500 million London action. A late-August filing led to a worldwide freezing order; newly public scheme details are allegations, not a finding of fraud. Here documentation authenticity and recoverable assets, rather than broad spread direction, determine the claim.

## Inflation data and buyback details will test the reopening

September 10 PPI consensus is +0.4% headline and +0.3% core monthly, with initial claims at 205,000 after 206,000. September 11 CPI is expected at +0.4% after +0.1%, core +0.2% and annual core 2.4% from 2.5%. Broader non-energy pressure favors September 16 Fed action; softer core and labor evidence would support waiting. The September 10 ECB and September 17–18 BOJ meetings test different domestic conditions. Japan's expected 25-basis-point move to 1.25% leaves subsequent pace especially important after wages.

September 9 buyback details precede the September 10 operation in 10- to 20-year Treasuries, alongside the September 9 ten-year and September 10 thirty-year auctions. The commitment implies at least $4 billion. Wrightson's Lou Crandall sees $5 billion–$6 billion as plausible; Morgan Stanley estimates a practical financing ceiling near $10 billion. Additional bills, a lower cash balance, the offer and actual acceptance are distinct. Disappointment could unwind anticipatory relative-value support, including in long-end swap spreads.

Amazon could price sterling from September 9. SoftBank's September 14–17 meetings are non-deal despite considering $10 billion–$20 billion of junk financing. Actual terms will test demand for the next supply. Senegal's $33.7 million September 13 payment on its 2048 foreign bond tests cash delivery while negotiations continue. Sophos commitments are due September 22 after a September 10 call; broad loan demand alone cannot settle that extension.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
Fresh attacks outweighed the first visible Qatari LNG exit since July. US business and household confidence weakened, while inflation expectations did not rise uniformly. Canada's retaliatory tariffs became effective.

Japan's wages strengthened, but consumption was flat and foreign flows differed across insurers and pensions. Australia showed broad strain; China's exports outpaced domestic auto demand.

US IG issuers raised $38.6 billion and loan borrowers pursued repricings and acquisitions. UK long funding cleared at a record DMO-era yield. Senegal's scenarios, Vista's asset sales and Sophos's extension still depended on specific creditor agreements.
overall_summary.summary: The 2- and 10-year yields rose 2 basis points to 4.39% and 4.80%, while 30-year yields gained 1 to 5.25%. Ten-year real yields held at 2.43%; breakevens rose to 2.37% as Brent reached $99.49.
